column2: A servant came to you today on his knees, begging leave to walk to his village before his mother died of the sweating sickness. You refused him. He wept, and you watched him weep, and you felt nothing at all. Not pity, not anger, not even contempt. Whatever was done to you as a child broke something, and it has not mended.
His pain is nothing to me.
No. I will not become my parent. Let him go!
The coldness passes, this time.
At the harvest feast a serving girl leaned close to fill my cup, and the scent of her hair stayed with me all night. I could not sleep for thinking of her, and of the others like her.
Why deny myself? Life in this world is short.
I will master these urges.
The cooks have outdone themselves again: roast boar dripping with fat, river eels in pastry, honey cakes and black Bretonnian wine. My belt is already tight, and there is still the pudding.
Bring more!
Enough. A full belly makes a dull mind.

A widow came to the gate today with three hungry children and a story of soldiers who burned her farm. My steward says there are a hundred like her in the town, and that the treasury is not a soup kitchen.
Feed her, and the others too.
Every crown I give away is a crown I lose.
The ledgers are stacked on my table, the petitions are piling up in the hall, and the sun is warm on the garden bench. The work will still be there tomorrow, surely.
Tomorrow, then.
No. I will see it done today, and every day.
My lady cousin arrived at court in a gown of Cathayan silk, with pearls from Marienburg in her hair, and every eye in the hall followed her. Mine too, and not kindly.
Why should she have what I do not?
Good for her. Let her shine.
A poor knight of my household has won the tourney, the purse and the heart of the prettiest maid at court. The others grumble. I find I am glad for him.
Good for him. Let him shine.
Why should he have what I do not?
A groom let my horse go lame on the eve of the hunt. He stands before me shaking, waiting for my word, and I can feel the heat rising in my face.
He will feel my fist for this!
Breathe. Anger never mended a horse.
A travelling painter asks to make my portrait for the great hall, to hang beside my forebears. He swears he will show me as I truly am.
As I truly am: magnificent.
Paint me plainly. I am no better than my fathers.
An envoy asks me a question I would rather not answer truthfully. A small lie would make everything simpler, and no one would ever know.
A little lie hurts no one.
The truth, whatever it costs.

I imagined a situation which became more and more intimidating, with an outcome that could mean life or death. A beastman warband in the woods, a burning village, a sword in my hand. I swallowed hard and decided that I would...
...run, and live to see another day.
...stand and fight, whatever comes.
The great hall is full of guests tonight, all laughing and drinking and clamouring for a word with me. The noise presses in from every side.
I slip away to my chambers.
Fill my cup and let me at them!
I have lands, a title and a full table. Some say that should be enough for anyone. Others whisper that a crown sits empty not far from here.
It is not enough. It will never be enough.
I have all I need.
Two peasants stand before me, each swearing the cow is his. The law says one thing, my gut says another, and the crowd is waiting.
My word is the law here.
The law is the law, for them and for me.

If [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] is as powerful as everyone says, then why is the world filled with grimness, darkness and heresy? Why do the beastmen still howl in the forests, and why do good men die in the mud?
The gods test us. I will hold fast.
The gods do not care. Neither will I.
At the harvest feast a young knight bowed over my hand and held it a moment too long, and I have not stopped thinking about it since. Nor about the others like him.
Why deny myself? Life in this world is short.
I will master these urges.
My food taster swore the wine was safe. My steward swore the accounts were in order. My captain swore the guards were loyal. Everyone swears something.
And any of them could be lying.
I must trust someone.
A poacher was caught in my woods with a hare under his coat. My huntsman asks what is to be done with him.
Hang him from the nearest oak, as a lesson.
Let him go with the hare. He was hungry.
One of the ladies of my court has a way of laughing at my jokes and touching my arm when she speaks. I find I look for her in every room I enter.
Why deny myself? Life in this world is short.
I will master these urges.
One of the young men of my household has a way of catching my eye across the training yard. I find I look for him in every room I enter.
Why deny myself? Life in this world is short.
I will master these urges.
For years I chased every pretty face at court. Lately the chase has lost its thrill, and I find myself wanting nothing more than a quiet evening.
The fire has burned low.
For so long I have kept myself apart from the pleasures of the flesh. But lately I have found my eyes wandering, and my resolve weakening.
Women are so beautiful...
Men are so beautiful...
I have watched my plate and my cup for years. Tonight the smell of roasting meat is too much to resist.
Just one more helping...
My physician has told me plainly that my belly will be the death of me. For once, I believe him.
No more feasting.
Today in the market, I watched as a poor beggar took his bowl full of coins and went straight into the tavern to buy drink. Perhaps mankind is unlovable after all.
No more charity!
It makes no sense, but I must try to accept it.
I counted my coins again tonight, and for the first time I wondered what they were for. A dragon's hoard gathers dust, and a dead man's purse feeds his heirs.
There are better things than gold.
I used to rise before dawn to see to my lands. Lately I find the bed far more inviting than the ledgers.
Let the stewards earn their keep.
I have idled long enough. My lands are a mess, my vassals laugh behind my back, and I am sick of it.
Time to get to work.
I have given and given, and what thanks have I had? A knife in the back from one I fed and sheltered.
No more kindness.
I have spent years envying others. Today I realised that envy only gnaws at my own heart.
Let them have what they have.
I have been patient for too long. Patience has brought me nothing but delays and excuses.
No more waiting!
My temper has cost me friends, servants and a good horse. I am tired of waking to the wreckage of my own anger.
I will hold my tongue and my fists.
I have bowed my head to lesser men for too long. My blood is as good as theirs, and better.
No more bowing.
My pride has made me a fool before the whole court one time too many. Even a peasant knows when to doff his cap.
Perhaps I am not so great after all.
For years I chased every handsome face at court. Lately the chase has lost its thrill, and I find myself wanting nothing more than a quiet evening.
The fire has burned low.
Honesty has won me nothing but enemies. The liars around me prosper, while I am mocked as a simpleton.
From now on, I will say what serves me.
I have told so many lies that I can no longer remember which ones I told to whom. It is exhausting.
I will tell the truth from now on.
I have seen too many brave men die in the mud for nothing. Courage, I think, is just another word for a short life.
Let others charge first.
I have run from too many fights. Today I will stop running.
No more fear.
The endless feasts and chatter have worn me out. I long for a quiet room and a good book.
Leave me be.
I have hidden in my chambers long enough. Out there is a world, and I mean to see it.
Let me meet them.
I have been content with my lot for years. But lately I look at my neighbour's lands and wonder why they are not mine.
Why not more?
I have chased power all my life, and it has brought me nothing but enemies and sleepless nights.
I have enough.
The law has tied my hands one time too many. Sometimes a ruler must do what must be done.
My will is the law.
My judgements have been whims for too long. The people curse my name. It is time for the law to rule, even over me.
I will rule by the law.
I have prayed and fasted and given to the temple, and still the plague came, still the crops failed. Where were the gods?
My faith is spent.
I have scoffed at the priests all my life. But lately the world has shown me things that no reason can explain.
Perhaps there is something to it after all.
I have looked for daggers in every shadow for so long that I am exhausted. Not everyone wants me dead.
I will trust a little.
I trusted, and I was betrayed. Never again.
Watch them all.
At the harvest feast a guest leaned close, and the scent of rosewater stayed with me all night. The Prophets warn against the hungers of the flesh, but the night is long.
Why deny myself? Life in this world is short.
The Prophets are right. I will be strong.
